site.title: Migration, Violence, and Gender Norms in Nepal

papers.title: Remitting Violence
papers.card_blurb: Does exposure to destination-country gender norms change attitudes toward and experiences of violence against women?
papers.question: Does exposure to destination-country gender norms change attitudes toward and experiences of violence against women?
papers.author: Bishal Chalise
papers.abstract: International labour migration exposes sending communities to the gender norms of destination countries. This paper asks whether that exposure changes attitudes toward, and experiences of, violence against women in Nepal. I combine labour-permit records, which fix the destination composition of each district's migrants, with time-varying indices of destination measures against violence against women and of legal gender equality, in the shift-share design of Godlonton and Theoharides (2025): the treatment is baseline migration intensity interacted with the share-weighted destination index, lagged two years. Outcomes come from the Nepal DHS 2001 to 2022 (wife-beating attitudes of women and men, household decision-making, experienced intimate-partner violence), INSEC human-rights records on sexual-violence incidents by local government (2020 to 2025) and district-court cause lists (2016 to 2025). Estimation is by OLS with district and year fixed effects and district-clustered standard errors. Exposure to stronger destination anti-violence policy leaves women's attitudes unchanged and raises men's acceptance of wife-beating slightly, while reported intimate-partner violence in the past year rises. Administrative records point the other way: recorded sexual-violence incidents and rape and domestic-violence cases per capita fall, and divorce filings rise, consistent with changes in reporting and exit from violent marriages rather than in underlying incidence. The administrative families have no comparable pre-period and are read as post-period exposure designs.

papers.title: Gendered Diffusion of Norms
papers.card_blurb: Do norms diffuse differentially for men and women? Evidence from international migration
papers.question: Do norms diffuse differentially for men and women? Evidence from international migration

hierarchy.label: C. Women’s economic and household roles

papers.author: Bishal Chalise
papers.abstract: Does international migration transmit gender norms across countries, and does it matter whether the migrants are men or women? Using Nepal's labour-permit records to fix the destination composition of male and female migration from each district, and the World Bank Women, Business and the Law index as a time-varying measure of destination legal gender equality, I estimate the Godlonton and Theoharides (2025) shift-share design with male and female migration entered jointly: each channel's baseline intensity is interacted with its own share-weighted destination index, lagged two years. Outcomes are individual-level, from the Nepal DHS 2001 to 2022: children's schooling by sex, marriage age and fertility, women's employment, decision-making and spousal gaps, and, for 2022 only, mental health and menstrual restrictions. Estimation is by OLS with district and year fixed effects and district-clustered standard errors. Norm transmission runs mainly through women's migration. Districts whose women migrated to destinations with improving legal gender equality see higher modern contraceptive use, later marriage and fewer child marriages, fewer children, more schooling among young women, fewer menstrual restrictions and fewer depression and anxiety symptoms, while the same exposure through men's migration moves these outcomes little. Daughters' school attendance and women's employment respond to men's migration instead. The findings are exploratory and sensitive to the thin female-migration network.

shifters.definition: World Bank Women, Business and the Law 1.0 composite score (0–100): unweighted mean of the eight indicator groups.
shifters.transformation: share-weighted district mean, then z-scored across the district × year panel 2001–2026 within share window × channel
shifters.sign_convention: higher = more legal gender equality at the destination.
shifters.scaling: 1 unit of Z = 1 permit per 1,000 residents × 1 SD of the share-weighted index
shifters.exclusions: India; destinations without a score in year t−2 (shares re-normalised)
shifters.motivation: Norm-diffusion channel: exposure to more gender-equal legal environments.
shifters.identifying_assumption: Destination legal reforms are unrelated to district-level trends in Nepal other than through the corridor.

shifters.definition: WBL 1.0 marriage indicator group (0–100): constraints on marriage, divorce, domestic violence legislation, obedience, household headship.
shifters.sign_convention: higher = fewer legal constraints on women within marriage.
shifters.motivation: Domain most directly related to household norms and violence.

shifters.definition: Mean of the WBL 1.0 workplace and pay indicator groups (0–100): job restrictions, sexual-harassment law, equal pay, industry and night-work limits.
shifters.source: World Bank WBL 1.0 panel, gr2_workplace and gr3_pay
shifters.sign_convention: higher = more equal access to work and pay.
shifters.motivation: Work-related norms that migrants observe directly in destination labour markets.

shifters.definition: UN Women Global Database on Violence against Women: composite index (0–100) of measures in force (laws, policies, budgets, institutional mechanisms, services, perpetrator programmes, prevention, monitoring, research, regional initiatives).
shifters.source: UN Women Global Database on VAW (clean: migration/vaw_policy_country_year_wide.rds, column vaw)
shifters.sign_convention: higher = more destination measures against violence against women.
shifters.exclusions: India; destinations without an index value in t−2
shifters.motivation: Violence-specific norm/policy environment at the destination.
shifters.identifying_assumption: Destination anti-VAW policy adoption is unrelated to district trends in Nepal except through the corridor.

shifters.definition: UN Women VAW database: policy-measures sub-index (0–100): laws, policies, budgets, institutional mechanisms, monitoring (excludes services, programmes and research).
shifters.source: UN Women Global Database on VAW, column vaw_policy
shifters.sign_convention: higher = more policy measures in force.
shifters.motivation: Policy-relevant component of the VAW index (cf. mig-vaw-norms lawpol variant).

shifters.definition: Mean of the seven working-age WBL 1.0 domains.
shifters.notes: Superseded in the UI by the marriage and work sub-indices (2026-08-20).
